findings.text: follow-on: _session_host_waiting reads reader-presence as host liveness, so a host that still holds its FIFO descriptor open while not serving is predicted host, whereas the real dispatch _ask_session_host_for_follower (dispatch.py:1415) writes a request and waits WATCHER_LOAD_BOUND_SECONDS for the session to attach before falling back to monitor; the dry run can therefore overstate delivery for a wedged host. The increment now records this limitation in the function docstring rather than closing it, which is correct -- telling a wedged host from a live one would need the one write a dry run must not make.

item_verdicts.call_sites: verified the changed capability's call sites in the reviewed head: _open_request_fifo at dispatch.py:1350 (the liveness read) and dispatch.py:10129 (the request write), _session_host_runs_follower at dispatch.py:6173 (dry run) and dispatch.py:7553 (real dispatch).
item_verdicts.diff: read the increment commit by commit against the previously reviewed head 413c5a025: one commit 97f58edfa corrects _session_host_waiting's docstring and routes it through the newly extracted _open_request_fifo (dispatch.py:10100), adds the host-census mirror branch at dispatch.py:6173 with the two parity tests, and updates the fragment lead.
item_verdicts.done_when: plan a-follower-lives-as-long-as-its-session s10 asks that a dry run for an unattached session with a waiting host FIFO finds no watcher-required refusal, a predicted delivery of host, and no byte written to the FIFO (tests/test_dispatch_session_host.py:377). The increment adds the sibling parity cases: tests/test_dispatch_session_host.py:448 (host-started follower -> host) and tests/test_dispatch_session_host.py:479 (hand-armed follower -> monitor); I ran the file at the reviewed head and it is 8 passed EXIT=0.
item_verdicts.goal: the increment extends the dry-run prediction so it mirrors BOTH arms of the real host admission, not only the waiting-host arm: reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6170 predicts host for a waiting host (as at 413c5a025) and dispatch.py:6173 adds the host-census arm, so a session a follower already runs reads host when the host's own census names that follower and monitor otherwise -- which is the delivery the real admission at dispatch.py:7543/7553 reaches for the same state.
item_verdicts.manifest: read the reviewed run's manifest: status complete, commits 413c5a025 and 97f58edfa, after_suite 61 passed EXIT=0 at 97f58edfa (gate-head.log), baseline_suite the declared negative control 1 failed EXIT=1 (gate-negative.log), negative_control_log named, and an empty follow_ons/blockers.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the increment 413c5a025..97f58edfa touches exactly the three declared paths -- reckon/crew/dispatch.py, tests/test_dispatch_session_host.py and the evidence fragment -- 86/62/2 changed lines, 117 insertions and 33 deletions; nothing outside them was written.

justifications.durability: the new cases assert from the code's output (resolution.watch delivery and session_attached) at dispatch.py:6173 and redden when that branch is removed; the waiting-host case independently asserts zero bytes read back off the FIFO.
justifications.evidence: independently ran tests/test_dispatch_session_host.py at 97f58edfa -> 8 passed EXIT=0 (review-gate-head.log), and independently reproduced the declared negative control by deleting the mirrored branch in a scratch extraction -> the host-started test fails monitor vs host EXIT=1 (review-negative-control.log), so the new guard is shown to fire.
justifications.fit: dispatch.py:10100 follows the module's docstring-and-type-hint idiom, the helper is private, and no name or comment carries a plan label, ticket number or version tag; the docstring records the mechanism (the shared reconnect-or-fall-back open) rather than a changelog.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the dry run now reports host for both states the real admission does -- a waiting host (dispatch.py:6170) and a follower the host's census names (dispatch.py:6173) -- and monitor otherwise, matching the real branches at dispatch.py:7543 and dispatch.py:7553; the two new tests assert the same fixture reaches host/monitor in the dry run as the pre-existing real-dispatch tests do.
justifications.reuse: the increment removes the duplication the previous review flagged: the non-blocking O_WRONLY|O_NONBLOCK reconnect-or-fall-back open that _write_fleet_request owned is now the single _open_request_fifo (dispatch.py:10100) shared by the request write and the dry run's liveness read, so the two spellings can no longer drift.
justifications.scope_discipline: the increment diff 413c5a025..97f58edfa is confined to the three declared paths, 117 insertions and 33 deletions, with no drive-by edits and no change to the real dispatch path except the shared _open_request_fifo extraction.
